{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Inspect the data
print(df.dtypes)
print(df.head())

# Check for the 6 QA orders with revenue 999999.99
print('\nQA orders count:', (df['revenue'] == '999999.99').sum())

# Convert revenue from string to float, removing commas
# First, check if any revenue values have unexpected formatting
print('\nUnique revenue values (first 10):', df['revenue'].unique()[:10])

# Clean revenue: remove commas and convert to float
df['revenue_clean'] = df['revenue'].str.replace(',', '').astype(float)

# Verify the clean conversion
print('\nSample of cleaned revenue:', df['revenue_clean'].head())

# Check for refunded orders
print('\nStatus distribution:', df['status'].value_counts())

# Filter out refunded orders (they should not count toward revenue)
df_filtered = df[df['status'] == 'completed']

# Check for QA orders in filtered data
qa_in_filtered = (df_filtered['revenue_clean'] == 999999.99).sum()
print(f'QA orders in completed orders: {qa_in_filtered}')

# Remove QA orders from filtered data
df_final = df_filtered[df_filtered['revenue_clean'] != 999999.99]

# Group by channel and sum revenue
channel_revenue = df_final.groupby('channel')['revenue_clean'].sum()

# Print result
print('\nChannel revenue (after cleaning, removing refunds and QA):')
print(channel_revenue)

# Find the channel with the most revenue
max_channel = channel_revenue.idxmax()
max_revenue = channel_revenue.max()

print(f'\nChannel with most revenue: {max_channel} ({max_revenue:.2f})')"}
